notes: Currency is not determinable from this file: no currency/CCY/waers column exists, and the only signal is a '$' prefix inside the Net price values ('$1234.56'). The target /currency is critical and defaults to THB, while the glyph points at USD. Per the rules, currency must not be inferred from a symbol or brand, so /currency stays unresolved — one question for the operator: which ISO currency should these net prices carry (free text, no FX conversion)?

SKU is stored with 4 leading zeros ('00470001') but the CSV profiler read the column as int, min 470001. The value must be re-read as text (source precision preserved, no strip_leading_zeros, no zero-padding added) so /sku emits '00470001'; treating it as an integer would silently corrupt the identity key.

Tax rate 5% on every row is an explicit fixture value and conflicts with the schema default 0.07 for /prices/*/vat_rate; the source value 0.05 is used because it is written in the data, and no Thai 7% convention is applied.
'Tax included' = 'No' for all rows means /prices/*/vat_included=false; no vat_adjust is applied because no target field requires VAT-inclusive amounts — the inclusion flag is simply passed through.

Price list is a single constant 'standard' (12/12), which also equals the contract default, so each SKU produces exactly one /prices entry with identity keys (/price_list, /effective_from); effective_from and effective_to have no source column and are correctly left null rather than fabricated.
Sales unit is a single constant 'PCS' already inside the unit.sell enum_hint; /unit/pack_size has no source column, so it is omitted rather than guessed as 1.

No inventory, promotion or category columns are present in this workbook, so /inventory, /promotions and /category are simply absent from the source — a coverage gap to report, not a reason to invent rows.

tables.reason: Sheet 'export' is one flat product list: 12 rows, one per SKU (SKU and Product name are both 100% distinct, unique_ratio 1.0), plus a single embedded price per product (Net price, Price list, Tax included, Tax rate). No warehouse/stock, promotion or category columns exist, so the price columns are attributes of the product row rather than a separate pricing table; role 'products' with an inline /prices entry is the best fit.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header 'SKU' is an explicit synonym of /sku; 12/12 distinct values 00470001–00470012, matching the contract's identity key and barcode_like/zero-padded example '000123'. The profiler typed the column as int (min 470001) because the leading zeros were consumed on read, so the mapping must read it as text to keep '00470001' intact rather than emitting 470001.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Header plus values ('SIM neutral 1'…'SIM neutral 12') are product display names, one per SKU, no nulls and fully distinct — the required /product_name field.

columns.name: Sales unit
columns.reason: Header 'Sales unit' is a listed synonym of unit.sell; the single distinct value 'PCS' is already in the contract's enum_hint for /unit/sell_unit, so no unit_normalize inference is needed. Constant across rows = one base unit for the whole list.

columns.name: Price list
columns.reason: Header 'Price list' matches the price.list_name synonym and the only value is 'standard', which equals the schema's own default for /prices/*/price_list; it is a required sub-field of each price entry, so each row yields one price with price_list='standard' exactly as the operator statement says.

columns.name: Net price
columns.reason: Header 'Net price' is an enumerated synonym of price.amount; 12/12 non-empty numeric values 1234.56–1356.77 formatted with a '$' prefix ('$1234.56', '$1279'). Amount is unambiguous, but the currency is not carried by any column of this file — the '$' glyph is display formatting, not a confirmed currency, so currency must stay unresolved (see notes) rather than be inferred.

columns.name: Tax included
columns.reason: Header is the price.vat_included synonym; single distinct value 'No' for all 12 rows, so every price entry is vat_included=false. This is explicit source evidence, not a retail-convention guess.

columns.name: Tax rate
columns.reason: Header 'Tax rate' matches price.vat_rate and the values are literal percentages ('5%', flagged percent by the profiler), so parse_number_th with percent_to_fraction yields 0.05. This fixture rate is explicit source evidence and overrides the schema default of 0.07; it is recorded as a stated fact, not an assumption about current tax law. Confidence is slightly lower than the other price columns because the pair (Net price, 'Tax included'=No, 5%) implies the amounts are VAT-exclusive, which matters for downstream semantics and should be confirmed only if the contract needs an inclusion decision.
